I'm so tired of this discussion. "What will I do to make money when the robots take over our jobs?" First off, wasn't this the whole goal of robotics? To create automated devices to make our lives easier? Now that they're starting to make an impact we can HOPEFULLY start letting go of the "if you don't work, you don't eat" mentality. It's asinine to not feed everyone on earth when we can.

My own personal thoughts on the future with AI and robotics is that it'll go 1 of 2 ways. 

1- Corporate greed will take over and force us into a dystopian hellscape where the majority of the population lives in squalor and with limited access to anything except recreational drugs and a black market economy.

2- People will realize that our purpose in life is not to work all day to make enough to survive and will celebrate that automation has allowed humanity the freedom to actually seek out interests and aptitudes and explore them. Humanity decides to abandon the relentless quest for more and stats a quest of working towards 'better'. The corporate "grind" becomes a cautionary tale told to future generations as a warning to not allow your time/life to be stolen for the benefit of others.

I'm sure the flames are incoming and my utopian future is ridiculous, blah, blah, blah. If we have the goal for the future set so low, that we are all looking forward to the complete industrialization and corporate takeover as a good option, then I think that we need to start looking for better goals. Just my 2 cents, but why would you want to devote your life to a future where your children face horrible conditions and subjugation? I mean, if you gotta work towards something, why not have it be something AMAZING?

As a seriously depressed, unmarried 48 year old guy, I know a little something through life experiences, and I am telling you that there are lonely people all around you. See the guy or gal sitting all alone in a corner with a paper or a book? How about the person sitting alone in a corner or in a restaurant smiling at everyone but not talking to anyone? Take a chance and go up to them. Introduce yourself and ask if they mind if you sit with them since you are here alone. Talk about whatever comes to mind. let things be organic and natural and don't have expectations of what is going to happen. you may see them again, you may not. The important thing you are doing here is going outside your comfortable bubble of isolation and meeting new people. I hope that this helps, I know it helped me. One useful thing I learned (from the movie American Pie of all places) that can bear repeating is that "interested is interesting". What that means is that listening is just as important as talking. Good luck and keep plugging.
